entries.note: DOI -> Throsby 2008 PLoS One (PMID 19079604, Dec 2008). Quote verbatim in abstract. untested correct. model_first_use_year 2008 is a judgement (C179 mouse protection predates, never a candidate); accepted.

McBride 2017 AAC (PMID 28807912). Quote verbatim. Healthy volunteers, not patients: see rule question 1. Full-text Intro cites mouse/ferret protection (ref 11) but Discussion makes no comparison, so comparison_stated=false stands. NCT01980966 has no posted results; registry_date null correct. Fix judgement: window chosen to 'reflect anticipated dosing practice', animal therapeutic window was 72 h, not 24-36 h.

Lim 2020 AAC (PMID 32393496, print Jul 2020). Quote verbatim. Discussion sentence 'In vivo rodent models and the human challenge study demonstrated MHAA4549A activity, both alone and with OTV' confirmed, followed by 'Despite these findings... did not appear to have antiviral activity beyond that of OTV': the paper's own comparison. Exposure statement confirmed (tracheal aspirate 500-600 ug/ml, 'R. Deng, unpublished data'). Registry results posted 2018-06-18 confirmed. Wording: CRANE Intro says 'additive effect with OTV'; 'synergy' is Nakamura 2013's word, attribute or soften.
Friesen 2010 PLoS One (PMID 20161706). Quote verbatim in abstract. untested correct; ferret dose-ranging for CR6261 with no human arm.

Gupta 2016 mAbs (PMID 27031797, online 31 Mar 2016). Quote verbatim. Full text: 'projected human efficacious dose of 45 mg/kg... was confirmed in patients in a Phase 2a study' cites ref 24 = Tavel J, 5th ESWI Influenza Conference, Riga 2014 (conference talk) and '(data not shown)'; Phase 1 CL verification cites ref 19 = ICAAC 2015 abstract. Neither peer-reviewed at the time; first peer-reviewed phase 2a data = McBride 2017 (phase 1 = Lim 2016 AAC, after Gupta). Gupta's 'in patients' is loose: the Phase 2a was healthy-volunteer challenge, so subjects=healthy_volunteers is right. Status same holds under rule 1 as written (peer-reviewed paper states the comparison) but see rule questions 1-2. Set confidence low, not medium. Judgement incomplete: McBride shows 400 mg (~5 mg/kg, below the projected range) significant on both assays (qPCR -46% P=0.046; TCID50 -62% P=0.009, unadjusted) while 1,200 mg was not; dose-response was non-monotonic, so 'only the upper bound held' overstates the fit. within_2x still defensible.
Same source and quote as engagement 1; verbatim, untested correct. Opener choice (2008 over C179 1990s) is a stated judgement; accepted.

McBride 2017. Quote verbatim in abstract. Symptom/mucus reductions are at 3,600 mg in healthy challenge volunteers: rule question 1. comparison_stated=false correct. Hershberger 2019 VIS410 claim in judgement not checked (budget); it carries no status.

Lim 2020. Quote verbatim. Paper itself frames the miss ('why the phase 2a influenza HVC study results did not translate into clinical benefit'), supports source_calls_it=miss and comparison_stated=true. Trial terminated at interim as unlikely to show benefit: 'stopped for futility' fair. Note wording: Intro says 'additive effect with OTV', not 'synergises'. Attribution of failure to timing/host/lower airway is in the paper; see rule question 3.

Gupta 2016. Quote verbatim in abstract. untested correct: no published animal-vs-human safety comparison; no FDA review exists (no approval), model_filed=false right. VIS410 GI/cytokine claims (Hershberger 2019, Sloan 2020) in judgement not checked (budget); non-status-bearing.

missing: Dose cell could anchor the PK half of Gupta's projection on peer-reviewed human data: Lim 2016 phase 1 (doi:10.1128/AAC.00607-16, epub Jun 2016) reports human CL/t1/2 in healthy volunteers vs Gupta's cyno-projected ~2.60 mL/day/kg; not checked whether Lim 2016 itself states the comparison.

Dose cell has no 2020 entry; defensible because status does not change (CRANE confirmed serum + tracheal exposure at 3,600 and 8,400 mg, so the exposure prediction held), but a note on the dose-2 entry saying so would make the strip self-explaining.

Han 2021 (CR6261 inert in H1N1 challenge, doi:10.1093/cid/ciaa1725) and Lim 2022 OFID (outpatient monotherapy, doi:10.1093/ofid/ofab630) are cited in judgements only; both reinforce contra and need no new entry. No peer-reviewed VIS410 hospitalized phase 2b found either.
rule_questions: Healthy-volunteer challenge as 'patient results': engagement 2, efficacy 2 (McBride 2017) and dose 2 (Gupta 2016, whose 'Phase 2a in patients' was the healthy-volunteer challenge NCT01980966) all rest on inoculated healthy volunteers. The brief defines same via 'patient results' yet provides subjects=healthy_volunteers as a recordable value, which implies they are scorable. If HV does not count: engagement and efficacy strips become 2008 untested -> 2020 contra, and dose becomes untested throughout (2010 only), since CRANE confirmed exposure but tested no dose prediction.

Comparison against unpublished clinical data: Gupta 2016 is a peer-reviewed DOI paper that states the dose comparison, but the patient-side evidence it cites is a 2014 ESWI conference talk, a 2015 ICAAC abstract and '(data not shown)'. Rule 1 as written is satisfied (the source making the comparison is peer-reviewed). If the patient-side result must itself be peer-reviewed, dose 2 moves to 2017 with McBride 2017 as source, comparison_stated=false (juxtaposition with Gupta's projection), and the quote must change.

contra when the source attributes the failure to conditions the model never tested: CRANE blames unknown infection-to-treatment interval, older comorbid hosts and lower-airway virus. The brief's contra ('the model predicted wrongly') still fits because rodent + HVC predicted activity with OTV and patients showed none, but the brief does not say whether 'wrong because never asked' scores contra or untested-in-patients.

Year basis: CRANE results were posted on ClinicalTrials.gov 2018-06-18 (first submitted 2018-05-18), two years before the paper. House convention (print_year) gives 2020; a registry-date convention would move both contra entries to 2018.
